prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1453; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record in this exercise, so let's just say the plaintiff.

Q: Understood. Where were you on the day of the accident?
A: I was driving home from work, stopped at a red light on a main road in Pearland, Texas.

Q: What happened while you were stopped?
A: I was struck from behind by another vehicle. I felt a hard jolt, my head snapped back, and then forward, and my seat belt locked against my chest.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, though it took me a minute. My lower back was already tight and I had a sharp ache when I stood up.

Q: Did anyone call for help?
A: The other driver called the police, and an officer came out to take a report. I also asked for an ambulance to check me, but I was not transported.

Q: When did you first seek medical treatment after the collision?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that same evening. They examined my back, took some X-rays, and told me I had a muscle strain.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've been going to physical therapy about three times a week. I was also prescribed muscle relaxers and an anti-inflammatory, and I see my primary care doctor for follow-up visits.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. Sitting for long stretches makes the pain worse, and I wake up some nights with stiffness across my lower back.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: I used to coach my kid's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to hand that off to my wife. Lifting groceries is hard, and I've had to stop going to my gym for a while.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I missed several days right after the accident, and since then I've been working a modified schedule with fewer hours at my desk, and I take breaks to stand and stretch.

Q: Before this collision, did you have any prior problems with your back?
A: No, not that I can recall. I'd had the occasional tweak from yard work, but nothing that needed a doctor.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your answers today?
A: Only that I want to get back to normal, and I'm hopeful the therapy will keep helping.
